1. Storage in the existing append-only room files (rooms.py; same segments, rollover, torn-tail quarantine, index and lock rules as slice 1)
- New line kind "item": {schema_version, sequence, operation_id, kind:"item", item_kind:"requirement"|"decision"|"question", title, author, created_at, text}.
- New line kind "item-event": {schema_version, sequence, operation_id, kind:"item-event", target_sequence, event:"accept"|"reject"|"amend"|"answer", state:"accepted"|"rejected"|"amended", author, created_at, text, record}. "record" is the pointer (below) for an accepted requirement/proposal/decision and null otherwise; text is the reject reason, the amended body, the answer, or an optional accept note. The item states are exactly proposed, accepted, rejected, amended, superseded.
- Rules: an item starts proposed. accept -> accepted with record; reject -> rejected; amend -> amended with the new title/text current, and the item may then be accepted or rejected; a later item line may name an older item in optional supersedes, which makes the older one superseded and refuses its acceptance. A question is answered with event answer -> state accepted, with answered_by/answered_at in the view; it stays a room item. accepted/rejected/superseded are final for accept/reject/amend.
- Idempotency: an accept uses deterministic operation ids derived from room id, item sequence and the item's current revision (not the client key) for both the record write and the item-event write. The record route's own journal and the room segment's operation-id check then make a repeated or concurrent accept converge on one record and one event; the first accepting person is the one recorded. The client Idempotency-Key still guards the HTTP mutation. Reject, amend and answer use the same item-derived rule.
- A moderated item (a tombstone targets its sequence) cannot be accepted, rejected, amended or answered: 409. moderate will accept an item as a target as well as a message. Its title/text is served nowhere, including the new index cache.
- Reads: read_messages keeps the paged log (item and item-event lines carry their sequences and appear in order) and adds "items": current item views for the room - item_kind, state, title, current text, who posted and when, decision history (who/when/what), record pointer and the orchestra:room/<rid>#<seq> evidence text. The view comes from a new derived "items" cache in index.json; a missing or stale cache is rebuilt from the segment lines, which stay the truth (as in slice 1), and the cache drops a moderated item's text on moderate and on rebuild. Bounds: title 1..200, body 1..max_message_chars (4000), reason <=500, plain-text rules as slice 1 (U+E0100 refused, reserved "Kind:" prefixes refused by the post path).

2. Accepted items become the kit's existing records, existing fields only
- requirement kind, accepted by a requirement editor (http_authority.requirement_editor: owner/coordinator session): backend.owner_requirements "create" then "accept" with item-derived operation ids, title = item title, description = item text + "\n\norchestra:room/<rid>#<seq>". The acceptance's usual native decision gets the same pointer appended to its rationale through an optional adapter argument used only by this route (no record shape change). Record pointer: requirement id, revision, sha256 (and the generated decision id).
- requirement kind, accepted by a contributor (a session that is not the requirement editor but holds proposals.write): a requirement proposal through the existing proposals route, as that person, target {"kind":"requirement-new"}, text = item text, rationale = item title, evidence = ["orchestra:room/<rid>#<seq>"]. No requirement is created; the pointer is in the proposal's existing evidence list. A viewer or a session without proposals.write is refused.
- decision kind, accepted by an owner or coordinator: a native decision issue from templates/DECISION.md (Decision / Rationale / Alternatives Considered, pointer in Rationale). I will factor the existing decision-creation code out of requirement_http.acceptance into one helper and expose a small service-only canonical action room-decision; requirement acceptance and room decisions then call the same builder (same labels, journal and guarded write). InProcessBackend answers 501 for it, as it already does for requirements.
- reject, amend and question answers create no record.
- No new record shape and no requirement "source" field. Tests validate created rows with the existing validators and assert the pointer appears only in the requirement description, the proposal evidence list and the decision rationale.

3. HTTP routes and authority (every POST is CSRF-protected by the existing route machinery; tests exercise that)
- POST /v1/projects/{pid}/rooms/{rid}/items {item_kind,title,text,supersedes?} -> 201; session member with CAP_ROOMS_POST (contributor+); agent credential refused as in slice 1.
- POST .../items/{seq}/accept -> session only, checked before any role or grant check (R7: even an agent credential holding the coordinator grant is refused); then requirement -> requirement_editor, or proposals.write for the contributor path; decision -> CAP_COORDINATE; question -> 400, use answer.
- POST .../items/{seq}/reject {reason} -> session only; same authority as accept for that kind.
- POST .../items/{seq}/amend {title,text} -> session only; same authority as accept; state amended, awaited again.
- POST .../items/{seq}/answer {text} -> session only; question only; any member with CAP_READ; records the answerer and time.
- Room reads keep the slice-1 refusal of agent credentials. Item writes are audited (rooms.item.post/accept/reject/amend/answer) and go through _mutate, the project lock for room appends, and the existing idempotency machinery. A moderated item, an archived room and an archived project keep their explicit refusals.

4. Web page (web/js/views/rooms.js, api.js, routes/app/css; dom.js textContent only)
- An item panel and a create-item form (kind, title, text, optional person asked) for contributors+; item state and decision history; Accept / Reject / Amend buttons shown only to the people who may decide that kind, Answer for questions; the record pointer shown as text; room text is always a text node, never innerHTML.
- Node DOM-shim test tests/web_rooms_items.mjs: markup and javascript: in item title/text render as inert text; a contributor sees Accept (proposal path) but an owner sees the requirement path; an amendment redraws; no element is made from room text.

5. Docs: docs/HTTP_DEPLOYMENT.md rooms section gains items, states, the routes/authority table with R7, the exactly-existing-fields pointer mapping, the shared decision builder and the rollback note: an older kit reads the created requirements, proposals and decisions unchanged; .388 room lines are newer than .385's reader, so a rollback to .385 names such rooms damaged rather than serving them, and a kit without rooms ignores .rooms entirely.

6. Tests
- tests/test_rooms.py additions: item/item-event line shapes, every state transition, supersede, amend then re-decide, idempotent accept, moderated item refused, index cache rebuild and no moderated text in index bytes, export includes items.
- tests/test_rooms_items_http.py: R7 credential with and without the coordinator grant refused on accept/reject/amend; contributor accept -> proposal, not requirement; owner/coordinator accept -> requirement and decision; accept twice -> one record and one event; moderated item cannot be accepted; pointer on every created record; CSRF on every decision route; text rules (U+E0100, reserved "Kind:" prefix, 200/4000 limits); archived room/project and non-member refusals; a question answer records who and when.
- tests/test_rooms_items_real_bd.py (goomba, real bd): requirement create+accept with pointer, decision issue from templates/DECISION.md, proposal submit, all read back; an older-kit-reads-unchanged check validates the created rows with the release base's existing readers/validators and asserts no field outside the existing shapes changed.
- tests/web_rooms_items.mjs as above.

Delivery: ~/work/delivery/kittrial-5bb.388-r1.bundle (new name each time, sha256) through the structured review route with the exact release base and commit.

- title 1..200, body 1..4000 (the max_message_chars setting), reason <=500; same plain-text rules as slice 1.
- A question answer is state accepted with event answer and answered_by/answered_at; a declined question is rejected.

- Agent credentials still cannot read rooms at all (slice 1), so R7 is enforced before any role or grant check.
- The index items cache is derived, never authoritative; deleting it loses nothing.

## b1: the record identity is the item's, not the caller's

**Today**, the requirement path writes through `owner_requirements`, whose operation id is `_result_key(principal, ...)`. That hashes the user id, so a retry by another person writes a second record. The proposal path goes through `invoke('proposals.submit', key=...)`, also hashed per caller. 1. **The intent decides, not the caller.** The accept intent line records:

   - `record_kind`: `requirement`, `proposal` or `decision`, chosen at the first attempt from that person's authority;
   - `parent`: the job chosen;
   - `content`: the digest;
   - `by`: who intended it.

2. **One native identity per item.**
   - `owner_requirements` and the proposal submit gain an explicit `record_identity`, used verbatim as the endpoint operation id (`room-record:` plus the identity plus `-create`, `-accept` or `-proposal`) in place of the caller-hashed `_result_key`.

   - a contributor fails, then an editor accepts: refused (cancel first), one proposal;

## b2: moderation always wins; no stuck items

1. **Moderation cancels.** Moderating an item with a pending intent:
   - appends an `item-intent-cancel` line (reason "moderated", by the moderator) before the tombstone, in the same room-lock section;
   - `pending_accept_intent` ignores cancelled intents;
   - a later retry of that identity is refused (409 `cancelled`) by `intend_accept` and again by `accept_item`.

2. **A coordinator can cancel an intent.** New route `POST .../rooms/{rid}/items/{seq}/intent/cancel` with a reason, for an owner or coordinator only. It writes the same audited cancel line, and the item returns to proposed or amended.
3. **Archive resolves pending intents.** Under the item lock, archive cancels every pending intent (reason "room archived") before the archive line, so nothing is left pending in an archived room.

6. **A native record already written before the cancel.** The cancel line records `record_may_exist: true` and the identity. The item's read shows it, and a coordinator can find and retire it. The record's evidence points back at the room line.

This is from reading the code: it is not exercised, because a proposal intent is now completed only by its author (Q2).
- **room-decision:** its journal key was the item's identity itself. So another coordinator's retry was refused for a different principal: stuck, but never duplicated.

**Consequence: the fix does not reuse ids across people.** Each person writes under their own id (`ApiHandler._room_decision_operation` for decisions), and a retry reads the earlier attempts' own rows in the endpoint journal through `EndpointBackend.prior_room_write` (http_service.py:3334). That row is written only by the endpoint, so a planted record or label can never match.

## b1: one record per item, whoever retries

- **The intent decides the record.** The intent line (`rooms.intend_accept`, rooms.py:442) records:
  - `record_kind` (requirement, proposal or decision, decided once from the first person's authority);
  - `content` (the digest);
  - `parent`.

  A retry writes exactly that.
- **Who may complete it** is checked live (`rooms_item_accept`, http_service.py:6894):
  - requirement or decision: a current owner or coordinator; a person demoted since is refused (403), never turned into a proposal (N3);
  - proposal: only its author (N5).

  A retry naming another parent is refused (409, N9).
- **Reading earlier attempts.** Before writing, the route reads every earlier attempt's outcome (`_room_prior_record`, http_service.py:6675):
  - committed: adopt the record (N1: one requirement and decision pair, not two);
  - a created but unaccepted requirement: the retrying editor accepts it;
  - recorded as refused: it wrote nothing;
  - in flight, unknown, expired, digest-only or **missing**: 409 until a coordinator cancels. Committed rows are kept about a day.
- **The attempt log.** A person's attempt is logged (`item-intent-attempt`, rooms.py:494) immediately before their own native write and only then. So a refused or adopting retry logs nothing and cannot make a later retry uncertain. At most five people try one intent.

## b2: nothing stuck; moderation always wins

- **Moderation** cancels a pending intent in the same room-lock section as its tombstone (`rooms.moderate`). With no pending intent it is exactly as before (tested). This covers N6 and N7: a contributor's failed accept never blocks the owner.
- **Archive** cancels every pending intent in the room first (`rooms.archive`, N2).
- **Owners and coordinators** cancel any intent through `POST /v1/projects/{pid}/rooms/{rid}/items/{seq}/intent/cancel {reason}` (http_service.py:7020). An intent's author may cancel only their own proposal-kind intent; viewers and others get 403.
- **The cancel line** (`item-intent-cancel`, `rooms.cancel_intent` rooms.py:528) names:
  - the identity;
  - `records`, the record ids known from the journal (the coordinator's Q1 answer: named because the journal maps them cheaply);
  - `record_may_exist` when any outcome is unknown.
- **After a cancel:** a cancelled identity is refused for ever, at both `intend_accept` and `accept_item`. The item's next acceptance gets a fresh identity that counts the cancels (`rooms.accept_identity`, rooms.py:386).
- **Namespaces** (N8, N8b):
  - intents and cancels are found by kind and identity, never by a bare operation id;
  - "already decided" means only that an accept or reject event of that item exists (`rooms.decision_event`, rooms.py:550);
  - client keys starting with `room-` or `intent-` are refused (422) on every room write route, messages included. That is checked once in `_rooms_project` for every POST and again in the rooms module (`check_client_operation_id`, rooms.py:326). One test walks all ten room write routes;
  - the web page's keys are `web-` plus a UUID, so it is unaffected. One test helper's default key `room-key-1` became `msg-key-1`.
- **A moderated item's** intent loses its recorded parent in the JSON-lines export.

**Deviation from the plan, stated:** a supersede stays **refused** (409 accepting) while an intent is pending, rather than cancelling it. Any member may post a superseding item, so a supersede that cancelled would let a contributor cancel an owner's acceptance in flight. Moderation (owner or coordinator), archive (owner or coordinator) and the cancel route are the ways out. M42 is now killed by a test of that refusal.
